{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study evaluates the predictive potential of a human GI microtissue model for drug-induced diarrhea, comparing its performance to clinical outcomes and providing quantitative measures of accuracy (84% and 83% in repeat experiments). It explicitly compares the in vitro model's predictions to human clinical data for a panel of drugs.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study evaluates drug-induced diarrhea, a gastrointestinal toxicity, and assesses the predictive potential of an in vitro model for this adverse event.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on gastrointestinal toxicities which can occur across various therapeutic areas, and the validation set includes drugs from different classes, not specific to one therapeutic area.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses a human GI microtissue model and compares its predictive performance to clinical data and also mentions comparisons to in vivo animal studies (rat and dog) and Caco-2 cell lines.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study mentions preclinical data from rat and dog studies and uses human-derived cells for the microtissue model. It also refers to mouse colon organ bath assays and general animal studies.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses TEER (Transepithelial Electrical Resistance) as a measure of barrier function, which is a biomarker, and also reports clinical diarrhea incidence as a hard outcome, thus mixing primary and secondary endpoints."
}
